we propose a novel approach, Risk Extrpolation (REx) for improving out-of-distribution generalization that is motivated by a robust optimization perspective, and show that variants of REX can recover the causal mechanism of the target, while also providing robustness to changes of the input distribution (covariate shift).

The main takeaway from our work is that
by focusing on the risk of a model on a set of training domains, we can improve its out-of-distribution robustness.

we can leverage the variation across training domains to build models that can generalize to a wider range of test domains, and that this approach is particularly effective when the test domains are more extreme than those seen in training.
